structure: Independent people sampled from a trivariate Gaussian population matching all supplied means, variances, and correlations. Gaussian shape is a modeling choice; all three requested population functionals are identified by the supplied second moments without it.

parameter_provenance.basis: Exact population means in X, Y, Z order.
Covariance equals Pearson correlation times both standard deviations; both standard deviations are one.
The reported correlations equal covariances because all variances are one.
Chosen joint shape for executable sampling; no record specifies higher moments or distributional shape. Independent people are stipulated by the task.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: Population OLS slopes on Z are both 0.6 and intercepts are zero. Residual covariance is 0.5 - 0.6*0.6 = 0.14; each residual variance is 1 - 0.6^2 = 0.64. Their Pearson correlation is 0.14/0.64 = 0.21875.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: Record A directly supplies the marginal population Pearson correlation.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: The population OLS slope with an intercept is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z) = 0.6/1.

limitations: Gaussian shape is an unmeasured scenario choice, not an additional evidentiary finding.
Finite-sample means, variances, Pearson correlations, and fitted OLS quantities fluctuate randomly; the generator performs no realized-sample calibration.
Residual correlation describes separate linear adjustments for measured Z. It is not a causal effect, and its identification here does not imply identification of arbitrary conditional relationships.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked covariance positive definiteness: leading principal minors are 1, 0.75, and 0.39, all positive.
Analytically checked the residual covariance and variances, giving partial correlation 0.21875.
No code execution or empirical sample checks were performed.
